haiku-low.q1: After the Message Service's transaction commits (step 4). The ack {msg_id, seq} tells the sender the message is stored with that sequence number.
haiku-low.q2: The sender gets an error and nothing is published. The retry must carry the same msg_id; the store then returns the original seq without inserting a new row.
haiku-low.q3: After 30 s without a heartbeat, when the presence key expires. Heartbeats every 10 s reset the TTL. A clean disconnect deletes the key immediately.
haiku-low.q4: The gateway requests a push after no ack in 5 s, and the Offline Inbox entry stays until the client acks that msg_id.
haiku-low.q5: The push failure is logged and not retried. The Offline Inbox entry is left untouched.
haiku-low.q6: Pending entries are fetched and bodies sent in ascending seq per conversation. Duplicates are dropped by the client using msg_id.
haiku-low.q7: The outbox row is committed in the same transaction as the message, so the relay still publishes it after a crash. Rows are deleted only after bus confirmation.
haiku-low.q8: In the Presence Registry, an in-memory key-value store mapping user_id to gateway node. The 30 s TTL expiry removes the entry when heartbeats stop.
haiku-low.q9: The worker sends the message to gateway G's delivery queue, and G writes it to the socket. The client's msg_id ack within 5 s confirms receipt.
haiku-low.q10: In the Offline Inbox, as per-user pending entries. Written for each recipient in step 8a before delivery. Removed on the client's msg_id ack, or after 30 days.
haiku-low.q11: It reads the user's pending Offline Inbox entries (R2), then fetches the message bodies by msg_id from the Message Store (R3).
haiku-low.q12: The event is never acked, so the bus redelivers it and another worker repeats the whole recipient list. Inbox puts are idempotent on (user_id, msg_id).

sonnet.q1: After step 3's single transaction commits (message inserted with seq and outbox row); the ack {msg_id, seq} tells the sender the message is stored with its assigned seq. It does not mean recipients have received it.
sonnet.q2: The sender gets an error; no outbox row is created, so nothing is published and no one receives it. The retry must carry the same client-generated msg_id; the store returns the original seq rather than inserting again.
sonnet.q3: After 30 s without a heartbeat the presence key's TTL expires (heartbeats every 10 s reset it), and the user then counts as offline.
sonnet.q4: Gateway G requests a push; the Offline Inbox entry stays (not deleted), so the message can still be delivered later (e.g. on reconnect).
sonnet.q5: It is logged and not retried; the Offline Inbox entry is untouched.
sonnet.q6: Per conversation in ascending seq. Duplicates are dropped by msg_id by the client (live messages during reconnect are placed by seq and de-duplicated by msg_id).
sonnet.q7: The message and outbox row are committed in one transaction, so the outbox row persists; the Outbox Relay later publishes it and fan-out happens. The client's retry gets the original ack.
sonnet.q8: In the Presence Registry, an in-memory key-value store mapping user_id to gateway node. The 30 s TTL removes the key if heartbeats stop (a clean disconnect deletes it explicitly).
sonnet.q9: The Fan-out Worker looks up the user in Presence Registry, finds node G, and sends the message to G's delivery queue; G writes it to the socket and starts a 5 s timer. The client acking the msg_id within 5 s confirms arrival (and deletes the Inbox entry).
sonnet.q10: In the Offline Inbox (per-user pending entries, pointers not bodies). Written by the Fan-out Worker for every recipient before any delivery attempt (step 8a). Removed when the client acks that msg_id (live or after reconnect); entries also expire after 30 days.
sonnet.q11: It reads the user's pending entries from the Offline Inbox (R2), then fetches the message bodies by msg_id from the Message Store (R3), and sends them per conversation in ascending seq.
sonnet.q12: The event was not acked, so the Event Bus redelivers it and another worker repeats the whole recipient list. Inbox puts are idempotent on (user_id, msg_id) and clients drop duplicate msg_ids.
